title: Introduce provider abstraction layer for VPC egress and CNI plugin modules
creator: Priya Kulkarni
description:
Problem: Our monolithic networking Terraform modules tightly couple egress (NAT/eip) and CNI configuration to cloud-provider-specific resources. This causes long apply times, frequent drift, and blocks cross-region + multi-cloud testing. We need to decompose the shared egress module, add a thin provider-abstraction layer, and upgrade the AWS provider to 5.x to pick up performance and drift fixes.

Goals:
- Split egress responsibilities into: control-plane routing (shared), provider-specific egress implementations (aws, gcp stub), and a provider-abstraction interface that workspaces consume.
- Reduce terraform plan/apply time for workspace changes by enabling targeted applies and smaller state churn.
- Upgrade aws provider and terrform provider pinning to reduce drift incidents caused by older provider bug.
- Ensure zero-downtime migration path with automated smoke checks and canary apply strategy.

Success criteria:
- 30% reduction in median tf apply duration for networking changes in staging;
- No >2 minute service-impacting downtime during migration in canary;
- PRs merged with tests and migration runbook;
- Post-migration 90-day drift alerts suppressed to baseline levels.

Approach / Implementation Plan:
1) Design interface: Define a minimal set of outputs/inputs for egress_abstraction (route tables, nat attachments, egress ip mappings). Document in Confluence: Infra - Egress Abstraction spec.
2) Create provider implementations: aws/egress_aws module that maps abstraction to nat gateway / eip / subnet attachments. Keep feature parity with current module but smaller scope. Add gcp placeholder module for future.
3) Provider layer: Add variables and a new root-level module wrapper that selects implementation by var.provider and validates required inputs.
4) Upgrade providers: Bump aws provider to 5.21.0 in root; centralize required_providers in shared versions.tf and test plan/apply in a dry-run pipeline.
5) Migration tooling: Author a migration script (terragrunt/Makefile) that performs staged moves of state resources into new module path using terraform state mv and state rm/imp as necessary.
6) Canary & rollout: Start with non-prod workspaces (dev1 -> dev2), run smoke tests and traffic routing checks, then staging, then prod with one region at a time.
7) Observability: Add tracer tags for apply correlator, instrument CloudTrail/Stackdriver log group queries for NAT resource churn, and add a dashboard with plan/apply durations.
